findings.namedBuyers: Verified commercially relevant contact candidates: Tamsyn Gilbert, PhD, Director of Program Development and Collaborative Partnerships; Alba Lopez Fahey, Conference Producer; and Mar Bianchi, Conference Producer, all at Common Ground Research Networks. Their roles support partnership/operations outreach, but neither assignment to this edition nor hotel purchasing/signature authority is verified. Route through support@cgnetworks.org or +1-217-328-0405. Stephen Sheps, Joe Recupero and AJ Cordeiro are the local academic committee, not established hotel buyers.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced eighteenth edition: 13–15 October 2027, Toronto Metropolitan University, Toronto, Canada, plus online. These are conference activity dates, not publication dates, and fall within the requested horizon. The special focus is Images After the Real: Synthetic Media, Networked Circulation, and Artificial Meaning. No 2028 edition announcement was located in the official pages/calendar reviewed; do not project dates or a Toronto return.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: a 157-room Harbourfront city hotel could serve a right-sized subset of nonlocal delegates, speakers or executives, but there is no evidence to size a block or qualify the event as too large or too small. Do not treat the full 157 rooms, a 15–109-room scenario, or any room-night total as demand. TMU is a separate downtown campus, not the nearby MTCC; MTCC walkability is not a venue-fit argument here. Main sessions already have a university venue. Accommodation is the primary plausible role, with side meetings only if separately requested. A resort pitch is not supported. The brand dining page lists breakfast at The View and a summer-only pool; it does not establish October 2027 catering capacity or lounge availability. Reconfirm all F&B before promising receptions.
findings.venueCommitments: Published venue: Toronto Metropolitan University, 350 Victoria St, Toronto, Ontario M5B 2K3, Canada. TMU identifies its campus as downtown Toronto: Toronto proper, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The specific conference building, meeting rooms and contractual terms are not published on the venue page. This is a publicly announced university venue, not proof of an executed venue contract or a hotel commitment.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified sequence: 2024 Buenos Aires / Interamerican Open University; 2025 Paris / Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne; 2026 Singapore / Nanyang Technological University; 2027 Toronto / Toronto Metropolitan University. The network explicitly describes an Annual Conference. This establishes annual recurrence and international university-host rotation, not annual Toronto hotel demand or a known 2028 destination.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific sourcing remains unconfirmed. The 2027 Hotel & Accommodations page contains only its heading and Common Ground contact footer; no hotels are listed, so there are no published edition-specific hotel names to enumerate. No room block, rate, booking deadline, housing bureau or open hotel RFP was identified. General organizer policy states: “Each conference secures discounted rates at selected hotels for delegates.” It immediately qualifies: “Common Ground facilitates the rate only and is not involved in booking. Participants are responsible for confirming reservations directly with hotels.” This is evidence of the general rate-facilitation/direct-booking model, not proof that any Toronto hotel has been selected, that inventory is committed, or that sourcing is open.
findings.organizationStructure: The Image Research Network is the scholarly network/programme; Common Ground Research Networks is the organizing umbrella and published contact organization; TMU is the announced university venue/local academic partner. Common Ground states it is an Illinois not-for-profit corporation, sustained by membership. This is a scholarly conference opportunity rather than a verified scaling-company event. No independent PCO, DMC, housing bureau or authorized contracting signatory was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No named incumbent hotel, guaranteed block, hotel shortage, sell-out, displacement or overflow demand was found in the edition-specific accommodation material. Absence of published hotels does not mean inventory is open. University-based sessions constrain a main-meeting-space pitch. Registration includes the welcome reception, coffee breaks and conference-day lunches, so do not assume these functions are contestable hotel revenue. Online participation also means total conference participation cannot be equated with traveling delegates.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Send a concise inquiry to support@cgnetworks.org for Alba Lopez Fahey or the producer actually assigned to The Image 2027; copy/request routing to Tamsyn Gilbert for a rate-listing partnership. Ask who selects recommended hotels, whether any Toronto hotels/rates or exclusivity already exist, and whether additional delegate-booked options are welcome. Request expected in-person nonlocal attendance, speaker lodging needs, stay pattern, room-night/peak-room expectations and booking/cutoff method before quoting a right-sized allocation. Offer lodging as the initial product, with no unsupported overflow or guaranteed-block claim. Confirm October 2027 F&B/meeting availability separately; do not lead with reception displacement.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the confirmed 2027 edition, hotel-rate/booking accessibility is unconfirmed rather than open or committed elsewhere. General policy makes a delegate-booked discounted rate arrangement a plausible discussion, subject to organizer confirmation. The confirmed university venue is not an invitation to replace the meeting site, and there is no sourced overflow requirement.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: pursue the confirmed Toronto 2027 lodging relationship first. Annual international rotation supports longer-term organizer relationship development, but no future Toronto return or 2028 local room demand is established. The published formal bid process concerns host-institution partnerships; it is not an open hotel lodging RFP. For later cycles, seek a hotel role only if a Toronto edition is announced or the organizer specifically requests it.
